question: In which of the following villages did the Chipko Andolan ('Hug the Trees Movement') originate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reni in Garhwal**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chipko Andolan** (or "Hug the Trees Movement") originated in the village of **Reni in Garhwal**, located in Uttarakhand, in **1973**.
 
• The movement was a grassroots environmental initiative aimed at protecting forests from commercial logging.
 
• Women, led by **Gaura Devi**, played a pivotal role by hugging trees to prevent them from being cut down.
 
• This movement became a symbol of environmental conservation and inspired similar movements across India and globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Andretta in Kangra:
 
• Located in Himachal Pradesh, Andretta is known as an artist’s village, famous for its pottery and cultural heritage.
 
• Ziro in Lower Subansiri:
 
• Situated in Arunachal Pradesh, Ziro is known for its scenic beauty and as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its unique Apatani tribal culture.
 
• Malana in Kullu:
 
• Malana, in Himachal Pradesh, is famous for its distinct culture and traditions, often referred to as one of the oldest democracies.
